request: We want to notify the right people when a freelancer's mission is about to end.

problem.value: Nobody is reliably warned before a freelance mission ends. The likely consequence is a missed renewal or extension decision, a late final invoice or validation, or an unmanaged handover.
problem.evidence: Request: 'notify the right people when a freelancer's mission is about to end'. The underlying pain is not stated and is inferred from the domain card (end-of-mission triggers notifications, final invoicing and validation).

current_process.value: Unknown. It could be manual tracking in a spreadsheet or calendar, ad-hoc reminders, or nothing.

existing_solutions.value: Unknown whether the platform's existing role-based notification mechanism could already cover this, perhaps by configuration alone. No budget or tooling is stated.
existing_solutions.evidence: The domain card says role-based notifications already exist as a key concept. Whether a scheduled or date-based reminder is supported is unknown.

success_metrics.value: Unknown. Candidates are no mission ending without a prior alert, renewals decided before the end date, and final invoices issued on time.

payer.value: A feature in an existing platform, so the payer is the platform owner or its clients. This is not a product idea.

actors.value: Recipients are 'the right people', not yet named. The candidates are the client's contacts (by role: operational, billing, HR), the internal manager or account owner, HR/admin, and the freelancer. The trigger is the system, driven by the mission end date.
actors.evidence: Request: 'the right people'. Context: Client contacts carry roles (billing, HR, operational) and notification routing depends on role.

business_objects.value: Mission (start and end dates, linked Freelancer and Client), Freelancer, Client and Contact (with role), and a Notification (event, recipient, channel, sent status).
business_objects.evidence: Domain notes on Mission and Client/Contact.

business_rules.value: Undefined: how long before the end ('about to end'), one reminder or several, which roles receive which message, and whether this varies by client, contract or country.
business_rules.evidence: Request: 'about to end' gives no lead time. Context: rules often vary by client, contract or country.

workflow.value: Mission lifecycle: start, running, approaching end (the new alert), ended (which can trigger final invoicing and validation). Open points: what action the recipient is expected to take (extend, renew, close, invoice) and whether the alert is informational or opens a task.
workflow.evidence: Context: end-of-mission is an event that can trigger notifications, final invoicing and validation.

integrations.value: Channel unknown (email, in-app, other). The trigger is likely a scheduled, asynchronous date-based check rather than an inline action. Unknown whether any external system (calendar, Slack) is involved.
integrations.evidence: Request says 'notify' without a channel. Context: notify implies who, when and which channel.

permissions.value: A notification must not reveal a mission to someone who cannot see it. For example, a client contact should only be told about their own client's missions, and the freelancer's rate or terms should not leak into the message.
permissions.evidence: Deduced from the context: permissions are often forgotten until acceptance, and Contact role drives routing and visibility.

config_vs_custom.value: Unknown whether the lead time and recipient roles are standard for all clients or configurable per client.
config_vs_custom.evidence: Context: notification routing is typically client-specific on this platform.

constraints.value: No deadline or dependency stated. GDPR applies to freelancer personal data in the messages.
constraints.evidence: Context: regulatory section (GDPR on HR data).

edge_cases.value: To settle: end date changed after the alert (extended or shortened), mission ended early or cancelled, the end date is already within the lead time at creation, no contact with the right role, the same alert sent twice, and a freelancer with several missions ending together.
edge_cases.evidence: Context traps: idempotency, incomplete source data, recipient role missing.

reporting.value: Possibly a record of what was sent to whom and when. No audit or compliance need is stated.
reporting.evidence: No compliance or traceability driver named.

acceptance.value: Not defined. A candidate scenario is that a mission ending in N days notifies the configured roles exactly once.

risks.value: Wrong or missing recipients, duplicate or missing alerts, and alert fatigue. Rollout can be staged, for example behind a flag for one client first.

acquisition.value: Not applicable. This is a feature rolled out to existing platform users.
acquisition.evidence: Internal platform feature, not a product idea.

questions.q: What goes wrong today when a mission ends? For example, a renewal is missed, the final invoice is late, or nobody is told. How is the end date tracked at the moment?
questions.why: High impact, and the real need determines the recipients, the timing and the message. It also tells us whether this is a reminder or the start of a bigger end-of-mission flow.

questions.q: Who exactly should be notified? Please give the roles, for example the client's operational contact, the client's billing contact, the internal manager or HR, and the freelancer. Should different roles get different messages?
questions.why: 'The right people' is the core of the request. Recipients derived from contact roles mean routing rules, and getting them wrong exposes missions to the wrong people.

questions.q: How long before the end should the alert go out, and is it one alert or several (for example 30 days, then 7 days)? What should the recipient then do, and should the alert simply inform or also track that someone acted?
questions.why: 'About to end' has no definition. The lead time and the follow-up expectation decide between a one-off email and a reminder with a tracked task.

questions.q: Does the platform's existing notification feature already send date-based or role-based alerts that could be reused? Through which channel should this go: email, in-app or both?
questions.why: Reusing an existing capability could shrink the build a lot. The channel affects effort and tone.

questions.q: Should the lead time and the recipient roles be the same for every client, or can each client set its own?
questions.why: Per-client rules turn a fixed schedule into a configuration feature with an admin screen and migration of existing data.

questions.q: If a mission's end date is extended, shortened or cancelled after an alert went out, should the earlier alert be withdrawn and a new one issued? Should anyone be told about the change?
questions.why: End dates move often. The expected behaviour decides how alerts are re-evaluated and prevents duplicate or stale notifications.

challenges.headline: Build versus reuse notifications
challenges.premise: A new notification capability needs to be built for mission end.
challenges.alternative: The platform already has role-based notifications. If it can fire on a date offset or be fed by a daily job emitting an 'approaching end' event, this may be configuration plus a small trigger rather than a new engine.
challenges.consequence: Building a parallel notification path duplicates routing and permission logic, and the two can drift apart on who is allowed to be told what.
challenges.recommendation: Have an engineer check, before any estimate, whether the existing mechanism can take a date-based trigger and which roles it can already address.

challenges.headline: A notification may not be enough
challenges.premise: Informing people is the goal, so a one-way alert is the whole feature.
challenges.alternative: If the real pain is a missed renewal, final invoice or validation, the alert could carry a clear expected action or a trackable task. This is a reasoning proposal, since the client has not said what recipients should do.
challenges.consequence: A purely informational alert can be read and ignored, leaving the original problem in place while the feature counts as delivered.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with the client what happens after the warning and decide whether acknowledgement or follow-up is in or out of this phase.

challenges.headline: One rule for every client
challenges.premise: 'The right people' and 'about to end' can be defined once for the platform.
challenges.alternative: Start with one default lead time and one default recipient set, and add per-client configuration only if clients actually ask. Routing is typically client-specific on this platform, so the default must be easy to override later.
challenges.consequence: Building per-client configuration up front adds an admin surface and data migration. Hardcoding without a seam forces a rewrite when the first client differs.
challenges.recommendation: Ask whether lead time and recipients differ across clients, then decide between a single default and a configurable build.

challenges.headline: Notification versus follow-up workflow
challenges.premise: A reminder that a mission is about to end is enough to make the end-of-mission work happen.
challenges.alternative: Treat the end-of-mission event as the start of a small checklist (extend, close, final invoice, validate) with a visible open/done state per mission, with the reminder as its first step. A reminder with no tracked outcome only tells you it was sent, not that anyone acted.
challenges.consequence: If the real pain is missed renewals and late final invoices, a notification alone can be sent, ignored and still leave no one accountable. Adding acknowledgement and follow-up later also changes the data model, so retrofitting is costlier than deciding now.
challenges.recommendation: Before estimating, ask the client what each recipient should do on receiving the message, and decide whether tracking the outcome is in scope for the first release.

challenges.headline: Building before checking existing notifications
challenges.premise: This needs a new notification capability.
challenges.alternative: The platform already has role-based notifications and a Mission end date. A reminder fed by those two may need only a scheduled trigger and a routing rule, not a new engine.
challenges.consequence: Building a separate mechanism duplicates routing and permission logic that is shared across modules, and creates a second place to maintain client-specific routing.
challenges.recommendation: Have an engineer review the current notification and routing features and confirm what can be reused before committing to a scope.

challenges.headline: Undefined 'right people' for external contacts
challenges.premise: The right recipients can be decided later and messages can carry the mission details.
challenges.alternative: Start with internal recipients only (account owner, HR) and add client contacts by role once the content of the message is agreed. Client contacts are external, so the message can be kept to the minimum, such as mission name and end date, with no rates or freelancer personal data.
challenges.consequence: A wrong or over-detailed message to an external contact could disclose rates or personal data of the freelancer, a GDPR exposure, and is hard to take back once sent.
challenges.recommendation: Agree who receives what, and what each recipient type is allowed to see, before the first send.

complexity_reasons: scheduled, asynchronous trigger with no duplicates
recipient routing by contact role, possibly per client
handling end-date changes and extensions after a reminder was sent
scope could grow into a follow-up workflow
briefs.cost_driver: recipient routing and handling of changing end dates
risks: Wrong or missing recipients: a client with no contact in the needed role, or a contact seeing data they should not (rates, freelancer personal data).
Duplicate or outdated reminders if an end date moves or a mission is extended after a send.
A first run on existing missions could flood recipients with notices for missions already near or past their end.
Notification routing and permission rules are shared across modules, so changes may ripple into other screens.
Scope creep from 'notify' into extension, final invoicing and validation workflows without an agreed boundary.

opportunities.text: Make the date-driven reminder generic (an event-and-offset trigger with role-based recipients) so other end-of-period events can reuse it.
Use the end-of-mission event as a shared trigger that final invoicing and validation can subscribe to later.
Reuse the client contact roles (billing, HR, operational) as the routing key, rather than creating a separate recipient list.

next_steps: Hold a short discovery conversation with the client to settle the timing (days before, one or several reminders), the recipients per role, the channel and what recipients must do.
Review the platform's existing notification and role-based routing features to determine what can be reused.
Agree a minimal message content per recipient type, with a privacy check on what external contacts may see.
Build a first slice: one reminder, internal recipients, with duplicate protection and date-change handling, then extend to client contacts once validated.

decisions.decision: The trigger is time-based and asynchronous, driven by the mission end date.
decisions.why: A reminder ahead of a future date cannot be inline with a user action.
decisions.alternative: A manually triggered reminder from a mission screen.
decisions.tradeoff: Needs scheduling, retries and a record of what was sent, in exchange for no reliance on someone remembering.

decisions.decision: Recipients are chosen by contact role and internal role rather than a fixed list.
decisions.why: The platform already attaches roles to client contacts and notification routing depends on them.
decisions.alternative: A hand-maintained recipient list per mission.
decisions.tradeoff: Depends on contacts having the right role recorded, in exchange for no per-mission upkeep.

decisions.decision: This is an internal feature of the existing platform, with no separate revenue model.

open_decisions: How many days before the end, and how many reminders

Channel: email, in-app or both

Success measure for the feature
